title: A Comparative Study on Betterment of Society through Corporate Social Responsibility Communication in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
venue: Ph.D. Dissertation, Kushabhau Thakre University of Journalism and Mass Communication
abstract: This doctoral study investigates the role of CSR communication in driving societal betterment across Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. Employing a mixed-methods design with 400 beneficiary surveys and 40 stakeholder interviews across 10 districts over a 5-year period (2018-2023), the research identifies a critical 26-point communication chasm in local dialect usage, highlights the superior efficacy of verbal communication channels, and proposes an original Five-Pillar Framework for CSR communication governance.
apa: Hashmi, S. A. M. (2026). A Comparative Study on Betterment of Society through Corporate Social Responsibility Communication in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (Doctoral dissertation, Kushabhau Thakre University of Journalism and Mass Communication).

title: Closing the CSR Communication Chasm: Language, Efficacy, and Stakeholder Engagement in Tribal Mining Belts
venue: Journal of Strategic Communication & Public Governance, Vol. 14, No. 2, pp. 112-135
abstract: Examining CSR communication in central Indian mining zones, this paper analyzes why printed materials fail to reach indigenous beneficiaries and demonstrates how vernacular verbal engagement increases trust scores by 42%.
apa: Hashmi, S. A. M., & Mandavi, A. (2025). Closing the CSR Communication Chasm: Language, Efficacy, and Stakeholder Engagement in Tribal Mining Belts. Journal of Strategic Communication & Public Governance, 14(2), 112-135.

title: The Five-Pillar Framework: A Normative Model for Evaluating CSR Governance Communication
venue: International Communication Gazette & Governance Review, Vol. 86, No. 4, pp. 245-270
abstract: Presents a operationalized model evaluating CSR communication across five core pillars: Strategy, Participation, Transparency, Feedback, and Impact Assessment.
apa: Hashmi, S. A. M., & Sharma, N. K. (2024). The Five-Pillar Framework: A Normative Model for Evaluating CSR Governance Communication. International Communication Gazette & Governance Review, 86(4), 245-270.

title: Comparative Analysis of Corporate Disclosure vs Community Perception in Central India
venue: International Association for Media and Communication Research (IAMCR) Annual Conference, Christchurch
abstract: Employed content analysis of annual corporate ESG reports and cross-referenced them with beneficiary perception data in 10 industrial districts.
apa: Hashmi, S. A. M. (2024). Comparative Analysis of Corporate Disclosure vs Community Perception in Central India. Presented at IAMCR Annual Conference, Christchurch.

title: Communication for Social Betterment: Re-evaluating Development Communication Models in Post-Industrial India
venue: Handbook of Global Development Communication (Routledge), pp. 88-104
abstract: Discusses theoretical evolution of communication for development (C4D) in the context of corporate social investment in emerging economies.
apa: Hashmi, S. A. M. (2023). Communication for Social Betterment: Re-evaluating Development Communication Models in Post-Industrial India. In Handbook of Global Development Communication (pp. 88-104). Routledge.
